goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

golden_verdicts.matched_finding: Slot end not checked against working hours end
golden_verdicts.reason: F16 (and F4) identify the same issue: slotStartTime used for both start and end in the working-hours check, so slot end is never validated against workingHour.endTime — matches 'incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime'

golden_verdicts.matched_finding: Object identity comparison on dayjs instances at line 114 is always false (dead code / incorrect guard)
golden_verdicts.reason: F0, F15, and F17 all identify the === comparison on dayjs objects at line 114 always being false, matching the golden comment about using === instead of .isSame()

findings.blocking_reason: The finding acknowledges the downstream isBefore/isAfter checks may still produce correct results for the common case, and does not concretely demonstrate that the zero-duration override produces an incorrect outcome in production.
findings.body: `checkIfIsAvailable()` uses strict equality (`===`) to compare two separately-constructed dayjs objects: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`. Each `dayjs()` call returns a fresh wrapper object, so `===` compares object identity, not value. This expression is *always* `false`, meaning the `return false` branch on the next line is unreachable dead code. The author almost certainly intended value equality (`.isSame()`). The intended semantics were to short-circuit when an override has zero duration (start === end) — that case is now silently bypassed, and the code falls through to the subsequent `isBefore` / `isAfter` checks instead. While the downstream checks may happen to still produce correct results for the common case, the guard is logically broken and masks the zero-duration override case, which will instead be handled by the `slotEndTime.isBefore(date.start.add(utcOffset))` branch in a way the author did not intend.
findings.evidence: Line 114: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))`. dayjs objects are referentially distinct on every construction; `===` on two distinct object references is always false per ECMAScript spec. No `.isSame()` is used. This is inside the newly-added `checkIfIsAvailable()` function introduced by this PR, so it is not pre-existing.
findings.suggestion: Replace with value comparison: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")))` — or better, compare the raw ISO strings of `date.start` and `date.end` directly (since the offset is applied identically to both, equality is preserved). Add a unit test with a zero-duration override (start === end) to lock in the intended behavior.
findings.title: Object identity comparison on dayjs instances at line 114 is always false (dead code / incorrect guard)

findings.blocking_reason: The finding speculates about both reachability (all three timezone sources being null) and about dayjs.tz behavior with undefined ("may throw" or may silently fall back), without concretely demonstrating a production crash or incorrect behavior; this is a defensive-programming opportunity, not a proven regression or broken contract.
findings.body: Line 212 calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` with no guard for `override.timeZone === undefined`. The PR adds `timeZone?: string` as an OPTIONAL field on `TimeRange`, so existing overrides persisted before this PR (and any new code path that forgets to set it) flow `undefined` into `dayjs.tz(date, undefined)`. The behavior of dayjs.tz with an undefined timezone argument is not guaranteed by the dayjs plugin contract — it may throw, return NaN offset, or silently use the host timezone, all of which produce incorrect slot availability. Because `getUserAvailability.ts` is the only confirmed producer wiring `timeZone` onto overrides (via the fallback chain at L201), any other producer (or a schedule with null timeZone AND null eventType.timeZone AND null user.timeZone) produces an override reaching this line with undefined. This is a backward-compatibility regression: code that compiled before the PR now has a new runtime failure mode.
findings.dimension_name: TimeRange.timeZone type contract, backward compatibility, and consumer coverage
findings.evidence: schedule.d.ts declares `timeZone?: string` (optional). slots.ts:212 dereferences without guard: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)`. getUserAvailability.ts:201 builds timeZone via `schedule?.timeZone || eventType?.timeZone || user.timeZone` — if all three are null (possible for users with no schedule, or legacy data), the override is pushed without timeZone and reaches L212 as undefined. Reachability: any COLLECTIVE/round-robin event where a member has no schedule.timeZone set and no eventType.timeZone fallback → undefined flows to L212.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit guard before L212: `if (!override.timeZone) { /* fallback to event/user timezone or skip tz-aware offset calc */ }`. Alternatively, make `timeZone` required on `TimeRange` and migrate all producers in a single PR, OR default `override.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone ?? inviteeTimeZone` at the call site. The type contract `timeZone?: string` advertises that undefined is acceptable, but the consumer at L212 contradicts that contract — one of them must change.
findings.title: override.timeZone dereferenced without undefined guard — legacy overrides crash

findings.blocking_reason: This is an incomplete fix for a new feature, not a regression — the per-override-timezone behavior is unchanged from before the PR, so no previously-working behavior is broken.
findings.body: The PR's stated goal for #8273 is to make fixed hosts' date overrides respected in round-robin events. The fix adds `timeZone` to the `TimeRange` type so each override carries its own timezone. However, `checkIfIsAvailable` at L107 computes `utcOffset` from the `organizerTimeZone` PARAMETER passed by the caller, NOT from `date.timeZone` on the override entry itself. At L492, the caller passes `schedule.timeZone` (the schedule's timezone) as `organizerTimeZone` — not the override's timezone. This means: if a fixed host's date override was created in a different timezone than their schedule's timezone (e.g. host travels and sets an override while in Tokyo but their schedule.timezone is America/New_York), the offset calculation at L107 uses the SCHEDULE timezone, not the OVERRIDE timezone. The `date.timeZone` field added by the PR is never read in this function. The type contract is wired but the consumer doesn't consume it — the #8273 fix is incomplete for the per-override-timezone case.
findings.dimension_name: TimeRange.timeZone type contract, backward compatibility, and consumer coverage
findings.evidence: viewer/slots.ts L107: `organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0` — `organizerTimeZone` is the function parameter, `date` is the override. L492: `checkIfIsAvailable({...schedule, organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone})` — caller injects schedule.timeZone as organizerTimeZone, never reads schedule.dateOverrides[*].timeZone. The `TimeRange.timeZone` field added by the PR is unused in this code path. Reachability: any round-robin event with a fixed host whose override timezone differs from their schedule timezone → wrong offset → wrong availability decision.
findings.suggestion: At L107, prefer `date.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone` when computing the offset: `const effectiveTz = date.timeZone ?? organizerTimeZone; const utcOffset = effectiveTz ? dayjs.tz(date.start, effectiveTz).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;`. This makes the override's own timezone authoritative when present, falling back to the schedule timezone for legacy overrides. Update the call site at L492 to stop overriding `organizerTimeZone` onto the schedule object if `date.timeZone` will be used, OR pass both and let checkIfIsAvailable choose.
findings.title: checkIfIsAvailable uses organizerTimeZone PARAM, not date.timeZone from override — #8273 fix incomplete for per-override timezones

findings.blocking_reason: This is a test coverage/extension concern, not a build break or correctness regression.
findings.body: The existing ROUND_ROBIN test (1040-1108) also uses `hosts: []` and no date overrides, so it can't be trivially extended — a new test is required that sets `isFixed: true` on a host and applies `IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride(...)`.
findings.title: Existing ROUND_ROBIN test cannot be trivially extended

findings.blocking_reason: Logic bug in working-hours validation is a correctness concern but doesn't meet the blocking bar: no build/test break, no security vulnerability, no data loss, no API contract break, and the finding doesn't establish this is a regression of previously working behavior.
findings.body: The working-hours check at slots.ts:141-142 uses `slotStartTime` for both `start` and `end`, so it only validates the slot's start minute, not full-slot fit. This is inconsistent with both the busy-range check below (lines 153-180, uses `slotEndTime`) and the getSlots builder (lib/slots.ts:90, enforces `slotStart > endTime + 1 - eventLength`).
findings.title: Working-hours check uses slotStartTime for both start and end

findings.blocking_reason: Missing test coverage for an edge case is explicitly non-blocking per the release bar.
findings.body: The PR description claims to fix #8273 (fixed hosts in round-robin events). The relevant production path is `getSchedule()` → `fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(a => a.user.isFixed)` → `fixedHosts.every(checkIfIsAvailable)`. The only round-robin test in this PR (`scheduleForRoundRobin`, lines 1032-1164) constructs the event with `hosts: []` (line 1107). With no fixed hosts, `fixedHosts` is an empty array and `fixedHosts.every(...)` is vacuously `true` — every slot passes the fixed-hosts filter without ever invoking `checkIfIsAvailable()` for a fixed host. The test therefore exercises only the loose-hosts path and never validates the timezone-aware date-override matching for fixed hosts. There is also no test that combines round-robin + `isFixed: true` hosts + a date override + a timezone difference between organizer and invitee — the exact scenario the PR claims to fix. The only `isFixed: true` fixture (line 867) is inside a collective (non-round-robin) event test with no date override. As a result, the regression for #8273 is not covered, and any future break of `checkIfIsAvailable()` for fixed hosts would pass CI silently.
findings.evidence: Line 1107: `hosts: []`. Line 485 in viewer/slots.ts: `fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter((availability) => availability.user.isFixed)`. `Array.prototype.every` on an empty array returns `true` (ECMAScript §22.1.3.5: 'every' returns true if array is empty). No test in the file sets `isFixed: true` on a user inside a round-robin (`schedulingType: 'round-robin'`) event with a date override. Grep for `isFixed` shows only line 867, which is in a collective event test (`scheduleForCollective` block, line 817).
findings.suggestion: Add a round-robin test fixture with at least one `isFixed: true` host, a date override on a different date than the regular working hours, and an invitee in a different timezone than the organizer. Assert that slots outside the override are filtered out for the fixed host while the loose-hosts path still returns availability. Also add a test with `hosts: []` but a non-empty fixed-host user pool to make the vacuous-truth behavior explicit and documented.
findings.title: Stated Bug 2 fix (fixed hosts in round-robin) is not regression-tested — round-robin test uses empty hosts array

findings.blocking_reason: This is a correctness bug in apparently new override-computation code with no evidence that cross-midnight handling previously worked and was regressed; it does not break the build, tests, security, data integrity, or an existing API contract.
findings.body:
The new override computation at lines 211–225 converts the override into `startTime`/`endTime` as **minutes-of-day** in the invitee's frame via `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + .minute()`. This extraction collapses the result into `[0, 1439]` and **discards the day component**. When `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` is large enough that the override crosses midnight in the invitee's local frame, `endTime` (in minutes-of-day) becomes **smaller** than `startTime`.

Downstream, `buildSlots` (line 68 `if (start >= end) continue;` and line 87 `for (let slotStart = boundaryStart; slotStart < boundaryEnd; ...)`) **requires `startTime < endTime`**. A crossed-midnight range is either skipped by the `start >= end` guard or produces a loop that never executes. The override is silently dropped — no slots are generated for it — and the user sees no availability for that period.

This is a common real-world configuration: a US organizer (e.g. America/Los_Angeles, UTC-8) with a 09:00–17:00 local override, viewed by an Asia/Kolkata (UTC+5:30) invitee. The override is stored as `09:00–17:00` UTC-encoded (organizer-local convention). Computation: `offset = 330 − (−480) = +810`. `startTime = (09:00 + 13.5h).hour()*60 = 22*60+30 = 1350`. `endTime = (17:00 + 13.5h).hour()*60 = 06*60+30 = 390`. Since `1350 > 390`, the range is dropped and **zero slots** are produced for that override — the invitee sees the override as if it never existed, falling back to regular working hours (which the override was supposed to replace).

The sign of `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` is itself **correct** for non-midnight-crossing cases — I verified analytically that the formula produces the right instant for positive/positive (IST→Dhaka), negative/positive (EST→IST), and positive/negative (IST→PST) configurations when the result stays within a single invitee day. The bug is the **lossy minutes-of-day representation**, not the sign. But because the only tested configurations are `+5:30` and `+6:00` (both positive, 30 min apart, never crossing midnight), this failure mode is completely unexercised.
findings.dimension_name: Sign/direction of offset across full offset spectrum; test coverage gaps
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `getSlots` (packages/lib/slots.ts:214) computes `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`. For organizer America/Los_Angeles (utcOffset=-480) and invitee Asia/Kolkata (utcOffset=330), offset = +810.
Step 2: lines 218–223 compute `startTime = dayjs(override.start).utc().add(810, 'minute').hour()*60 + .minute()` and `endTime` similarly. For a 09:00–17:00 organizer-local override stored as 09:00–17:00 UTC-encoded: startTime = (09:00+13.5h)=22:30 → 1350; endTime = (17:00+13.5h)=06:30 next day → 390.
Step 3: These are pushed into `computedLocalAvailability` (line 245) and passed to `buildSlots`.
Step 4: In `buildSlots`, line 68 `if (start >= end) continue;` skips this range (1350 ≥ 390), and even if it didn't, line 87 `for (let slotStart = 1350; slotStart < 390; ...)` would never execute.
Step 5: Result: zero slots generated for the override. The invitee sees no availability for the override period, silently falling back to (or being filtered out of) regular working hours.
findings.suggestion: Handle crossed-midnight override ranges in `buildSlots` by splitting them into two ranges: `[startTime, 1440)` and `[0, endTime]`. Alternatively, represent override boundaries as absolute minutes from `startOfInviteeDay` (allowing values ≥ 1440 or < 0) instead of minutes-of-day, so the existing loop works without modification. Either way, add tests covering: (a) organizer west of invitee (US → Asia) with a multi-hour override that crosses midnight in the invitee frame, (b) organizer east of invitee (Asia → US), (c) override that crosses midnight in the organizer frame.
findings.title: Overrides that cross midnight in the invitee's local frame are silently dropped — zero slots emitted

findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes a timezone consistency concern with speculative correctness impact near midnight boundaries but does not demonstrate a concrete failing test, regression, or production bug in this PR.
findings.body: Line 440 derives a single `organizerTimeZone = eventType.timeZone || eventType?.schedule?.timeZone || userAvailability?.[0]?.timeZone`. However, the three downstream call sites of `checkIfIsAvailable()` pass *different* values: line 492 (fixed hosts) passes `schedule.timeZone` (the per-user schedule timezone from the flattened override), line 517 (loose hosts) passes `userSchedule.timeZone`, and line 585 (per-user fallback) passes `userSchedule?.timeZone`. This means the `organizerTimeZone` used inside `checkIfIsAvailable()` — which drives both the `utcOffset` at line 107 and the `YYYY MM DD` date matching at line 110 — is NOT the event-level organizer timezone computed at line 440. For fixed hosts, if a host's `schedule.timeZone` differs from `eventType.timeZone`, the date-override matching will be performed in the host's schedule frame rather than the event frame the override was authored in. Date overrides are typically authored in the event/organizer timezone; matching them in a different frame can cause the `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format("YYYY MM DD")` comparison to land on a different calendar day than intended, especially for overrides near midnight or with large timezone deltas. The line 440 variable appears to be dead or used only for a non-display purpose, which is misleading.
findings.evidence: Line 440: `const organizerTimeZone = eventType.timeZone || eventType?.schedule?.timeZone || userAvailability?.[0]?.timeZone;`. Line 492: `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` (inside `fixedHosts.every`). Line 517: `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule.timeZone`. Line 585: `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone`. The value at line 440 is never passed to `checkIfIsAvailable()` in the fixed-hosts or loose-hosts branches — it is shadowed by per-schedule/per-user values.
findings.suggestion: Decide on a single source of truth for `organizerTimeZone` and use it consistently. Either (a) pass the line-440 `organizerTimeZone` to all `checkIfIsAvailable()` calls, or (b) document that per-user schedule timezone is intentionally used and ensure date overrides are authored/stored in that same frame. Add a test where `eventType.timeZone` differs from a fixed host's `schedule.timeZone` and assert the override still matches correctly. At minimum, remove or rename the dead line-440 variable if it is not used downstream.
findings.title: organizerTimeZone is inconsistent across call sites — fixed-hosts path uses per-schedule timeZone, not the event-level organizerTimeZone

findings.blocking_reason: The finding identifies a legitimate timezone-comparison correctness concern, but it does not concretely demonstrate that this is a regression from previously working behavior or that it meets any other specific blocking criterion.
findings.body:
The changed code compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` to `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` where `slotStartTime = time.utc()` (line 100). These two ends are NOT in the same time frame.

End A (changed location, line 110): `dayjs(date.start)` is called WITHOUT `.utc()` and WITHOUT `.tz()`. With the dayjs UTC plugin extended (packages/dayjs/index.ts:22), `dayjs(dateObj)` still parses a JS Date in the host server's LOCAL timezone — the default behavior is unchanged by extending the utc plugin; only `dayjs.utc(dateObj)` switches to UTC mode. So `.format("YYYY MM DD")` here yields the date in the SERVER's local timezone, offset by `utcOffset` minutes.

End B (the other end, line 100): `slotStartTime = time.utc()` is explicitly in UTC mode, so `.format("YYYY MM DD")` yields the UTC date.

Therefore the `===` comparison compares a server-local date (LHS) against a UTC date (RHS). The PROPERTY ("dayjs(date.start) yields a UTC-based timestamp consistent with slotStartTime = time.utc()") does NOT hold — they only coincide when the host server happens to run in UTC.

This also contradicts the adjacent line 107, which uses `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` and treats `date.start` as an instant interpreted in the organizer's timezone — a third frame. The same `date.start` is parsed three different ways within 4 lines: `.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` (line 107, instant-in-organizer-tz), `dayjs(date.start)` (line 110, server-local), and `dayjs(date.end)` (lines 114/118/123, also server-local).

The sibling implementation in packages/lib/slots.ts:219-223 confirms the intended frame: it uses `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` — explicitly `.utc()` — when computing override hours/minutes. The changed location omits `.utc()`, diverging from that established pattern.

Concrete consequence: on a server whose TZ is not UTC (e.g. TZ=America/Toronto in this environment), the LHS day-boundary is shifted by the server's own UTC offset relative to the RHS. Slots that legitimately fall on the override day in UTC (and in the organizer's timezone) can be classified as outside the override, and vice versa, causing `dateOverrideExist` to be set incorrectly and the override check at lines 133-135 / the early-return at 128-131 to wrongly include or exclude slots. The bug is silent on UTC-host deployments (e.g. typical Vercel/Docker UTC containers), which is why it likely escaped detection.
findings.evidence:
Changed location (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:100-111):
```
100:   const slotStartTime = time.utc();
...
107:       const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;
108:
109:       if (
110:         dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") ===
111:           slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")
112:       ) {
```

Other end — the UTC counterpart the code should be consistent with — is `slotStartTime = time.utc()` (line 100), which is UTC-mode. The sibling implementation in packages/lib/slots.ts:219-223 shows the correct, consistent pattern:
```
219: dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 +
220: dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),
221: dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 +
222: dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").minute(),
```
Note the `.utc()` call before `.add(...)` — absent in the changed location.

dayjs config (packages/dayjs/index.ts:2,12,22) extends the utc plugin but does NOT change the default `dayjs(dateObj)` parsing, which remains host-local:
```
2: import dayjs from "dayjs";
12: import utc from "dayjs/plugin/utc";
22: dayjs.extend(utc);
```
findings.suggestion: Make the LHS explicitly UTC before applying the offset and formatting, mirroring the sibling pattern in packages/lib/slots.ts:219. Replace `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` with `dayjs.utc(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` on lines 110, 114, 118, and 123 (and the same for `dayjs(date.end)`), so that the day-boundary comparison and the start/end comparisons are performed in the same UTC frame as `slotStartTime`/`slotEndTime`. Better still, compute the override bounds once in UTC up front (e.g. `const overrideStartUtc = dayjs.utc(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes"); const overrideEndUtc = dayjs.utc(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes");`) and reuse them, eliminating the repeated server-local parsing. Also reconcile the offset direction with line 107's intent — `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` — since applying a negated offset to a UTC instant to recover the organizer-local date is itself suspect, but that is a separate concern from the frame inconsistency reported here.
findings.title: dayjs(date.start) parses Date in host-local time, inconsistent with slotStartTime UTC frame and with the .tz() usage on the adjacent line

findings.blocking_reason: Missing optional field population is a code-quality/consistency concern with no demonstrated production breakage, data loss, or API contract violation.
findings.body: The canonical producer of overrides doesn't populate the new optional field; `getSchedule` re-augments locally. Any other consumer reading `.timeZone` gets undefined. Inferred return type hides the narrowing.
findings.title: `getUserAvailability` returns `dateOverrides` without `timeZone`

findings.blocking_reason: Finding identifies missing test coverage and hypothesizes edge-case correctness issues but does not concretely demonstrate a production bug, regression, or broken contract.
findings.body: In `getSlots()` the offset is computed as `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` (line 214) and applied via `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` (lines 219-223) to project the override into the invitee's frame. The override filter at line 207 bounds overrides by the *invitee* day (`startOfInviteeDay` … `endOf("day")`). The only test (`scheduleForEventOnADayWithDateOverrideDifferentTimezone`, line 788) uses organizer=Asia/Kolkata (+5:30) and invitee=Asia/Dhaka (+6:00), yielding `offset = +30` minutes — both positive and small. There is no test for: (a) negative offset (organizer ahead of invitee, e.g. organizer in Europe, invitee in Americas — `offset` negative, override projected to previous day), (b) large offset crossing midnight in the projected frame (e.g. organizer +14, invitee -10 → offset -24h, override start lands on the prior calendar day and the `.hour()*60 + .minute()` computation wraps), (c) DST boundary dates where `utcOffset()` flips between the override date and the slot date, (d) overrides whose *raw* start/end are on day N but whose *projected* start/end cross into day N+1 or N-1 in the invitee frame. For these cases, the line 207 invitee-day filter may drop a relevant override (if the projected time shifts it out of the invitee's local day) or keep an override whose projected `startTime`/`endTime` wrap past 1440 minutes, breaking the minute-of-day comparison downstream in `getSlots`. The combination of invitee-day filtering + minute-of-day projection is fragile across midnight.
findings.evidence: Line 76-79 of getSchedule.test.ts: only `Asia/Kolkata` (+5:30) and `Asia/Dhaka` (+6:00) defined. Line 788: the only cross-timezone test uses these two. Line 214 of slots.ts: `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`. Line 207: filter uses `startOfInviteeDay` bounds. Lines 219-223: `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour()*60 + .minute()` produces minute-of-day in [0,1440); a projected time that crosses midnight will wrap and produce a wrong range. No negative-offset, midnight-crossing, or DST test exists in the file.
findings.suggestion: Add tests for: (1) negative offset (organizer east of invitee) — verify the override is still matched and slot times are correct; (2) offset magnitude ≥ 24h (e.g. organizer +13, invitee -11) — verify midnight wrap in the projected frame is handled; (3) a DST-transition date for one or both zones — verify `utcOffset()` is evaluated at the correct instant and the offset doesn't drift; (4) an override whose raw end is past midnight in the projected frame. Consider replacing the minute-of-day projection with direct dayjs range overlap checks to avoid wrap-around entirely.
findings.title: Offset formula and day-bounding only validated for positive offsets — negative offsets and midnight-crossing untested

findings.blocking_reason: This is a boundary-condition correctness bug in slot availability at an exact instant edge case, not a demonstrated build break, security vulnerability, data corruption, API contract break, or regression with evidence that it was previously working.
findings.body:
The two boundary checks that determine whether a slot is OUTSIDE a date override (and thus unavailable) are asymmetric, leaving a gap at exactly `date.end`.

CHANGED END (lines 118-119, start boundary): `slotEndTime.isBefore(date.start) || slotEndTime.isSame(date.start)` — this is INCLUSIVE: a slot whose end exactly equals the override start is caught as "outside the override" → callback returns true → `dateOverrides.find()` is truthy → outer `if` fires → `return false` (slot unavailable). This is correct: a slot ending exactly when the override begins does not overlap the override interior.

SIBLING END (line 123, end boundary): `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)` — this is EXCLUSIVE: a slot whose start exactly equals the override end is NOT caught. `isAfter` is false when `slotStartTime === date.end`. Neither outside-check fires, so the callback falls through (returns undefined), `dateOverrides.find()` is falsy, the outer `if` is skipped, and line 133 `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` fires → the slot is marked AVAILABLE.

CONSEQUENCE: A slot that starts at the exact end time of a date override is incorrectly shown as available. For example, if an override replaces working hours with 09:00–17:00, a slot starting at exactly 17:00 (which extends to 17:00 + eventLength) is treated as within the override and bookable, even though it starts when the override ends and extends past it. The start boundary correctly excludes slots ending at 09:00, but the end boundary fails to exclude slots starting at 17:00. The `isBefore/isSame` on slotEndTime and the bare `isAfter` on slotStartTime do NOT together cover the entire outside region — there is a one-instant gap at exactly `date.end`.

Both branches trust the override equally (both set `dateOverrideExist` and use the same override object), so the inconsistency is purely in the boundary comparison operators, not in override handling.
findings.suggestion:
Make the end-boundary check symmetric with the start-boundary check by also excluding a slot that starts exactly at `date.end`. Change line 123 from:
`if (slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))) {`
to:
`if (slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")) || slotStartTime.isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))) {`

This mirrors the `isBefore || isSame` pattern used on slotEndTime at lines 118-119 and closes the gap at exactly `date.end`, so a slot starting at the override end is correctly treated as outside the override (unavailable).
findings.title: Asymmetric boundary check: slot starting exactly at override end (date.end) is treated as available when it should be unavailable

findings.blocking_reason: The midnight-crossing date-string comparison bug in checkIfIsAvailable appears to be pre-existing code that the PR's new call site exposes, not a regression of previously working behavior; the PR's fix is incomplete for this edge case rather than breaking something that worked before.
findings.body:
The two cluster findings combine into a single shipped regression that neither finding alone fully captures.

**Finding 1 (the bug):** `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:109-112) matches an override to a slot by comparing `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` where `slotStartTime = time.utc()`. Both sides are UTC dates. When an override spans UTC midnight (e.g. organizer in UTC setting 23:00–02:00, or any organizer whose local evening maps to a UTC-midnight-crossing window), a slot in the post-midnight portion of the override (e.g. 01:00 UTC on day D+1) has `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` = D+1, while `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format("YYYY MM DD")` = D. The string equality fails, `dateOverrideExist` is never set to true for that slot, and the slot falls through to the working-hours check (lines 137-151).

**Finding 0 (the safety gap):** The test fixture at apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:76-79 defines only `Asia/Kolkata` (+5:30) and `Asia/Dhaka` (+6:00). The only date-override test (line 742) exercises `offset = 0` and `offset = +30`. No test references any override that crosses UTC midnight, any negative offset, or any DST transition. A `grep` for `America/`, `Europe/`, `midnight`, `DST` in the override-related tests returns zero matches.

**The compound:** Finding 0's coverage gap is not a generic test-quality nit — it is the specific mechanism by which Finding 1's bug reaches production. The PR's primary advertised fix (#8273, labeled High priority) is the fixed-host date-override filter in round-robin events. That filter calls `checkIfIsAvailable` with `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` for each fixed host (line 492). For any fixed host whose override crosses UTC midnight, the post-midnight slots are NOT recognized as covered by the override, so they fall through to the working-hours check. The working-hours check (lines 138-151) then either incorrectly excludes the slot (if the UTC time falls outside stored working hours — the typical case, since the override was meant to expand availability outside working hours) or incorrectly includes it (if working hours happen to cover that UTC time but the override was meant to restrict). Either way, the fixed-host filter produces a wrong availability result for the PR's headline scenario.

Because the test suite exercises only +5:30/+6:00 with no midnight crossing, CI passes green while this regression ships. The combined risk is strictly greater than each finding alone: Finding 1 alone is a latent bug that QA might catch; Finding 0 alone is a coverage gap that might not matter if the code were correct. Together they are a silent regression in the PR's primary fix, with false CI confidence.

**Concrete trace (verified against source):** Organizer in UTC, override 23:00–02:00 UTC, invitee in UTC, round-robin event with one fixed host. `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, "UTC").utcOffset() * -1 = 0`. For slot at 01:00 UTC day D+1: `dayjs(date.start).add(0).format("YYYY MM DD")` = D; `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` = D+1; D ≠ D+1 → override not detected → `dateOverrideExist` = false → working-hours check runs → `start = 60`, `workingHour.startTime` = 540 (09:00) → `start < workingHour.startTime` → returns true → `checkIfIsAvailable` returns false → slot excluded. The 00:00–02:00 slots that the override explicitly makes available are filtered out, and a booking at 23:00–23:59 (pre-midnight, correctly detected) may proceed while 00:00–02:00 slots vanish — an availability pattern that contradicts the override's intent and the PR's claim.

**Additional note:** The same midnight-crossing class also affects the `getSlots` path (packages/lib/slots.ts:218-224), where `dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...` produces an endTime (e.g. 120) smaller than startTime (e.g. 1380) — an inverted range pushed into `computedLocalAvailability`. This compounds further but is outside the two cluster findings; it reinforces that the midnight-crossing class is a real, multi-site failure mode that the PR's test strategy does not exercise at all.
findings.evidence:
Step 1 (Finding 1, verified in source): packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107 — `const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;`. Line 110-111: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` where `slotStartTime = time.utc()` (line 100). Both format() calls yield UTC dates.
Step 2 (Finding 1 trace): For override 23:00–02:00 UTC with organizerTimeZone="UTC": utcOffset=0; dayjs("23:00Z").add(0).format("YYYY MM DD")=D; slot at 01:00Z day D+1 → slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")=D+1; "D" !== "D+1" → override not matched → dateOverrideExist stays false.
Step 3 (fallthrough): Lines 133-135 — `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` skipped. Lines 138-151 working-hours check runs on the post-midnight slot. Line 141-142: `const start = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute();` (both from slotStartTime, so start===end). For 01:00 UTC and working hours 09:00–17:00: start=60 < workingHour.startTime=540 → returns true → checkIfIsAvailable returns false → slot excluded.
Step 4 (Finding 0, verified in source): apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:76-79 — `const Timezones = { "+5:30": "Asia/Kolkata", "+6:00": "Asia/Dhaka" };`. Line 742 test calls getSchedule with timeZone=Timezones["+5:30"] and timeZone=Timezones["+6:00"] only. No test in the file constructs an override crossing UTC midnight or uses a timezone with a negative UTC offset.
Step 5 (compound): The PR's Bug 2 fix (#8273) at lines 483-499 filters availableTimeSlots via fixedHosts.every(...) calling checkIfIsAvailable with organizerTimeZone=schedule.timeZone. For any fixed host with a UTC-midnight-crossing override, the post-midnight slots are incorrectly filtered. No test covers this. CI passes. The regression ships.
Step 6 (reinforcement): packages/lib/slots.ts:218-224 — `dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour()*60 + ...` yields endTime < startTime for midnight-crossing overrides, producing an inverted range in computedLocalAvailability — the same bug class in the Bug 1 path, also untested.
findings.suggestion: Fix Finding 1 by replacing the date-string equality check (lines 109-112) with an instant-based range check: set `dateOverrideExist = true` when `slotStartTime.isBetween(dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes"), dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"), null, "[)") || slotEndTime.isBetween(...)` and return true/false based on the range, not on date-string equality. Separately fix line 114's `===` (object-identity on dayjs instances, always false) to `.isSame()`. Close Finding 0 by extending the Timezones fixture (apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:76-79) to include `America/New_York`, `America/Los_Angeles`, `Europe/London`, and `Asia/Kathmandu`, and add tests for: (a) organizer UTC override 23:00–02:00 with invitee in UTC and in America/New_York — exercises UTC-midnight crossing in both getSlots and checkIfIsAvailable; (b) organizer Asia/Kolkata, invitee America/New_York — exercises negative offset; (c) a DST transition date with an override created on the transition day. Without both the code fix and the test coverage, the PR's primary fix (#8273) remains silently broken for midnight-crossing overrides.
findings.title: PR's headline Bug 2 fix (#8273 — fixed hosts' date overrides in round-robin) silently breaks for overrides crossing UTC midnight, and CI exercises zero midnight-crossing cases so the regression ships undetected

findings.blocking_reason: This is a defensive-programming edge case requiring an unlikely combination of missing fields; the finding does not concretely demonstrate the scenario is reachable in production or that this PR introduces a regression.
findings.body: Line 201 builds `timeZone = schedule?.timeZone || eventType?.timeZone || user.timeZone`. For a user with no schedule (schedule = null), no eventType.timezone, and no user.timeZone set, this chain yields `undefined`. The PR's `getWorkingHours({ timeZone }, availability)` call at L210 and downstream override population at L228 then produces `TimeRange` entries where `timeZone` is not explicitly set. Because `schedule.d.ts` declares `timeZone?: string` (optional), TypeScript does NOT flag this — the type system considers the entry valid. But the consumer at `slots.ts:212` dereferences `override.timeZone` assuming it is defined. The type contract is permissive (optional) while the consumer is strict (required-at-runtime), and there is no type-level enforcement that overrides flowing from getUserAvailability carry timeZone. This is the classic optional-field trap: the type says undefined is OK, the consumer says it is not.
findings.dimension_name: TimeRange.timeZone type contract, backward compatibility, and consumer coverage
findings.evidence: getUserAvailability.ts L201: `const timeZone = schedule?.timeZone || eventType?.timeZone || user.timeZone;` — all three can be null/undefined in valid Prisma state (schedule is optional, eventType.timeZone is nullable, user.timeZone has a default but can be unset for legacy users). schedule.d.ts: `timeZone?: string` — optional, TypeScript allows omission. slots.ts:212 — dereferences without guard. The producer-consumer contract gap is type-invisible.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) narrow the `TimeRange.timeZone` type to `timeZone: string` (required) once all producers are updated, so TypeScript catches missing producers at compile time; or (b) add a runtime assertion in getUserAvailability before returning overrides: `if (!override.timeZone) throw new Error("override missing timeZone");` to fail fast at the producer rather than silently at the consumer; or (c) add a default `timeZone: "UTC"` fallback at L201 so the chain never yields undefined.
findings.title: timeZone fallback chain may yield null — overrides returned without timeZone reach slots.ts:212 undefined

findings.blocking_reason: This appears to be a pre-existing edge-case limitation in cross-midnight timezone handling, not a regression or a new production-breaking defect introduced by this PR.
findings.body: Lines 219-223 compute the override's `startTime` as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + .minute()`. This yields minutes-since-midnight in the invitee's timezone, but when the offset pushes the override across a day boundary, the hour wraps modulo 24 and there is no field tracking WHICH day the override lands on. Example: organizer in Asia (UTC+8) sets override at 9am local = 1am UTC; invitee in US (UTC-5) → offset = -780 min → override appears at 8pm the PREVIOUS day in invitee tz. `hour()` returns 20, `startTime` = 1200, but the override is attached to the invitee's CURRENT day's working hours (because L207 filtered it into today's window by UTC). The slot may render on the wrong day. The `TimeRange` type has `start: Date` which carries the full timestamp, but the downstream `getWorkingHours`/slot-generation path uses `startTime`/`endTime` as day-relative minutes, losing the absolute date. The PR adds `timeZone` but does not add a day-tracking field, so this coverage gap remains.
findings.dimension_name: TimeRange.timeZone type contract, backward compatibility, and consumer coverage
findings.evidence: slots.ts L219-223: `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + .minute()`. `hour()` returns 0-23, wraps modulo 24 with no day carry. L207 filters overrides into the invitee's day window by UTC start, but the offset shifts the effective local day. WorkingHours type uses `startTime: number; endTime: number` (minutes-since-midnight), no date component. Reachability: organizer UTC+8, invitee UTC-5, override at 9am organizer-local → offset -780 → invitee-local 8pm previous day.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) track the offset-adjusted date alongside startTime/endTime and filter slots by absolute timestamp, or (b) document that overrides crossing midnight in the invitee tz are unsupported and validate against them at override-creation time. The `TimeRange.timeZone` addition helps compute the correct offset but the `WorkingHours` shape (`startTime`/`endTime` as minutes) cannot represent cross-day overrides — consider whether `Schedule` entries for overrides should use absolute `Date` ranges instead of day-relative minutes.
findings.title: Cross-midnight overrides: startTime computed via hour() wraps without day tracking — slot appears on wrong day

findings.blocking_reason: The finding does not concretely demonstrate that a zero-length date override is reachable from a real user-facing code path, and the bug is a logic correctness issue rather than a build break, security vulnerability, or data loss.
findings.body: `===` on two separately-constructed dayjs instances is always false (object identity). The zero-length date override branch is dead code; a zero-length override will incorrectly make all slots that day available.
findings.title: Object identity comparison for dayjs instances

findings.blocking_reason: Missing input validation with no demonstrated reachable exploit path or concrete production impact.

findings.title: Slot end not checked against working hours end

findings.blocking_reason: Dead-code logic bug in a comparison is a correctness/quality issue but the finding does not demonstrate concrete production impact such as data loss or a behavioral regression.

findings.blocking_reason: The finding does not concretely demonstrate that a real caller actually passes undefined timeZone through this path; it is a defensive-programming suggestion with low confidence, not a proven production regression or data corruption.

findings.blocking_reason: Missing test documentation of pre-fix buggy expectation is a code quality suggestion, not a correctness or security issue.
findings.body: Bug 1 test asserts +5:30 and +6:00 return identical slots but doesn't document the pre-fix buggy expectation, making the regression intent implicit.
findings.title: Bug 1 test lacks documented pre-fix buggy expectation

findings.blocking_reason: Missing test coverage for edge cases is explicitly non-blocking per the bar.
findings.body:
The test fixture defines only two timezones, both positive and 30 minutes apart:

```typescript
const Timezones = {
  "+5:30": "Asia/Kolkata",
  "+6:00": "Asia/Dhaka",
};
```

The date override test (`Check for Date overrides`, line 742) only verifies two configurations: organizer IST with invitee IST, and organizer IST with invitee Dhaka. These two cases exercise `offset = 0` and `offset = +30` — a tiny slice of the offset spectrum.

**Unexercised configurations that the `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` formula is unverified for:**

1. **Negative offsets** (US/Europe timezones). `organizerUtcOffset` and/or `inviteeUtcOffset` being negative changes the sign of `offset` and exercises the `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, ...)` path with a negative addend. A sign error here would shift slots the wrong direction — but this is never tested.

2. **Organizer ahead of invitee** (e.g. organizer IST, invitee PST). All tested cases have the invitee ahead of (or equal to) the organizer. When the organizer is ahead, `offset` is negative, which is the untested direction.

3. **DST boundary dates.** `dayjs.tz(date, tz).utcOffset()` correctly computes the offset at the date's instant (so DST is handled per-instant), but no test verifies behavior on DST transition dates (e.g. US spring-forward in March, EU in late March). An override created before a DST transition and viewed after it (or vice versa) could produce a 15–60 minute skew if the offset lookup were wrong. The current code looks correct, but it is unverified.

4. **Midnight crossing** (see the important finding above). No test has an override that, after offset adjustment, spans midnight in the invitee's frame.

5. **Half-hour non-IST offsets** (e.g. Asia/Kathmandu +5:45, Asia/Kabul +4:30) — minor but these exercise the minute-arithmetic differently than the 30-minute IST/Dhaka pair.

The `offset` formula is directionally correct for the narrow positive-positive case tested, but the PR's risk surface explicitly calls out that "a sign error would only manifest in untested configurations." The test suite does nothing to close that gap.
findings.dimension_name: Sign/direction of offset across full offset spectrum; test coverage gaps
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:76-79` defines `Timezones` with only `Asia/Kolkata` (+5:30) and `Asia/Dhaka` (+6:00).
Step 2: The only date-override test (`Check for Date overrides`, line 742) calls `getSchedule` twice — once with `timeZone: Timezones["+5:30"]` and once with `timeZone: Timezones["+6:00"]` — both with the same organizer schedule in `Asia/Kolkata`.
Step 3: These two calls exercise `offset = 330 - 330 = 0` and `offset = 360 - 330 = +30` only.
Step 4: No test in the file references any timezone with a negative UTC offset, any DST transition date, or any override that crosses midnight after offset adjustment. A `grep` for `America/`, `Europe/`, `US/`, `Pacific/`, `-5`, `-8`, `DST`, `midnight` in the test file returns zero matches in the override-related test cases.
findings.suggestion: Add test cases that cover: (a) organizer in a negative-offset timezone (e.g. America/New_York) with invitee in a positive-offset timezone (Asia/Kolkata) — exercises negative `organizerUtcOffset` and large positive `offset`; (b) the reverse — organizer Asia/Kolkata, invitee America/New_York — exercises negative `offset`; (c) an override that crosses midnight in the invitee frame after offset adjustment (e.g. organizer America/Los_Angeles 09:00–17:00, invitee Asia/Kolkata); (d) a DST transition date with an override created on the day of the transition. Expand the `Timezones` fixture to include at least `America/New_York`, `America/Los_Angeles`, `Europe/London`, and `Asia/Kathmandu` to cover negative offsets, half-hour offsets, and DST.
findings.title: Test coverage only exercises +5:30 and +6:00 — no negative offsets, no organizer-ahead-of-invitee, no midnight crossing, no DST boundary dates

findings.blocking_reason: Dead code duplication with no importers and no production impact; this is a code quality suggestion, not a blocking issue.
findings.body: A parallel type declaration without `timeZone`; currently no importers (dead code), but latent import-path hazard. Suggest deleting and re-exporting from canonical.
findings.title: Duplicate `TimeRange` in `apps/web/lib/types/schedule.ts`

findings.blocking_reason: Reviewer acknowledges this is likely correct behavior; the finding is a test/coverage and documentation suggestion with no demonstrated production impact.
findings.body: Line 485: `fixedHosts.every(schedule => checkIfIsAvailable({...}))`. If `fixedHosts` is empty (e.g. a COLLECTIVE event where no member is marked `isFixed`, or a round-robin with all loose hosts), `Array.prototype.every([])` returns `true` by the vacuous truth property of the universal quantifier. This means ALL slots pass the fixed-host filter regardless of overrides. This is likely the CORRECT behavior (no fixed hosts = no fixed-host constraint = all slots valid), but the PR's #8273 fix is specifically about fixed hosts, so the COLLECTIVE-with-no-fixed-hosts case should be explicitly verified. If the business intent is that COLLECTIVE events require AT LEAST one fixed host's override to be satisfied, the current code silently bypasses that. The `TimeRange.timeZone` addition does not change this, but the PR's scope (fixed-host override handling) makes this a coverage gap worth flagging.
findings.dimension_name: TimeRange.timeZone type contract, backward compatibility, and consumer coverage
findings.evidence: viewer/slots.ts L484: `fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(a => a.user.isFixed)`. L485: `fixedHosts.every(...)`. `Array.prototype.every` on empty array returns `true` (ECMASpec). Reachability: COLLECTIVE event type with all members `isFixed: false`, or round-robin with no fixed members.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit comment at L485 documenting that empty fixedHosts is intentional (no constraint). If the business intent is otherwise, add `if (fixedHosts.length === 0) return false;` (or `return true` with a test) to make the semantics explicit. Add a test case for COLLECTIVE event with zero fixed hosts to lock the behavior.
findings.title: fixedHosts.every() on empty array returns true (vacuous truth) — all slots pass fixed-host filter for COLLECTIVE with no fixed hosts

findings.blocking_reason: The finding does not concretely establish that this midnight-boundary mismatch is newly introduced by this PR rather than pre-existing behavior, and the edge case requires overrides spanning UTC midnight in specific timezone combinations.
findings.body:
The override-to-slot matching at lines 109–112 compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` where `slotStartTime = time.utc()`.

`utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` shifts the override's stored UTC-encoded-local-time to the actual UTC instant. `slotStartTime` is the slot's actual UTC instant. Both `.format("YYYY MM DD")` calls therefore compare **UTC dates**.

This works when the override does not cross UTC midnight in the actual-UTC frame. But when an override spans UTC midnight (e.g. organizer in UTC setting 23:00–02:00, or organizer in America/Sao_Paulo setting 22:00–01:00 local = 01:00–04:00 UTC next day), a slot in the post-midnight portion of the override has a `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` that is **one day later** than `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format("YYYY MM DD")`. The comparison fails, `dateOverrideExist` is never set to `true` for that slot, and the slot falls through to the working-hours check — which may incorrectly exclude it (if working hours don't cover that UTC time) or incorrectly include it (if the override was meant to restrict, not expand).

This is the same family of midnight-boundary bug as the `getSlots` finding above, but on the `checkIfIsAvailable` side used for fixed-host filtering (Bug 2's path). The sign of `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(...).utcOffset() * -1` is correct (the `* -1` converts dayjs's positive-for-east convention to the "minutes to subtract to get actual UTC" direction), but the day-boundary string comparison is blind to the override crossing midnight.

Note: there is also a latent pre-existing bug on line 114 — `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset) === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset)` is an object-identity comparison on two separately-constructed dayjs instances, which is always `false`. This means the zero-length-override early-return never triggers. This is not introduced by this PR (the line uses the new `utcOffset` variable but the `===` pattern predates it), but it compounds the midnight issue because the range checks that follow rely on `date.start !== date.end` semantics that are partially broken.
findings.dimension_name: Sign/direction of offset across full offset spectrum; test coverage gaps
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107) computes `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`.
Step 2: Line 110 compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` to `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` where `slotStartTime = time.utc()` (line 100).
Step 3: For an override that crosses UTC midnight (e.g. organizer UTC, override 23:00–02:00 UTC, date.start=23:00 plus2, date.end=02:00 plus3), `dayjs(date.start).add(0).format('YYYY MM DD')` = `plus2`, but a slot at 01:00 UTC plus3 has `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` = `plus3`.
Step 4: The string comparison `plus2 === plus3` is false, so the override is not detected for the 01:00 slot. `dateOverrideExist` stays false, and the slot is evaluated against `workingHours` instead of the override — producing an incorrect availability result for any post-midnight slot in a UTC-midnight-crossing override.
findings.suggestion: Compare instants instead of date strings. Replace the `format("YYYY MM DD")` equality check with a direct range check: `slotStartTime.isBetween(dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'), dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'), null, '[)')` (and set `dateOverrideExist = true` based on that). This handles midnight crossing naturally. Separately, fix line 114's `===` to use `.isSame()` or remove the dead branch. Add a test where the override crosses UTC midnight and a slot sits in the post-midnight portion.
findings.title: checkIfIsAvailable date-string matching uses UTC-date of slot vs adjusted-UTC-date of override — mismatches when override crosses UTC midnight

findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes a pre-existing latent issue that the PR may increase exposure to but does not concretely demonstrate a new regression or production-impacting failure.
findings.body: Lines 110-112 compare `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` to detect whether a slot falls on the override's date. This is a string-based day comparison. When the utcOffset shifts the override's effective local date across midnight relative to the slot's date, the formatted strings differ and the override is not detected for that slot. Example: override at 11pm organizer-tz, offset pushes it to 1am next-day in the comparison frame → `"2025 06 30"` !== `"2025 07 01"` → override ignored → slot wrongly treated as unavailable (or available). This is pre-existing, but the PR's timezone-awareness change makes offset values more variable (per-override tz vs single organizer tz), increasing the surface for cross-midnight mismatches. The `TimeRange.timeZone` field enables per-override offsets but the day-matching logic was not updated to account for the new offset diversity.
findings.dimension_name: TimeRange.timeZone type contract, backward compatibility, and consumer coverage
findings.evidence: viewer/slots.ts L110-112: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. String format comparison, no timezone normalization on slotStartTime side. With per-override timeZone (PR change), utcOffset varies per override, increasing cross-midnight probability.
findings.suggestion: Replace string date comparison with absolute timestamp range check: compute the override's effective start/end as UTC timestamps after applying the offset, and check `slotStartTime.isBetween(effectiveOverrideStart, effectiveOverrideEnd, null, "[)")`. This is robust to cross-midnight and removes the format-string dependency. Alternatively, if the override is meant to cover a full day, compare `slotStartTime.date() === effectiveOverrideDate.date()` using dayjs date objects with `.isSame(other, "day")` after both are normalized to the same timezone.
findings.title: Day-boundary string match for override detection fails across midnight (latent, surfaced by PR's tz-awareness)
